title: Did wallet {{wallet}} attend {{eventName}} ({{eventStart}} to {{eventEnd}})?
description:
This case is about one guest of an event run with Proof of Presence, a refundable-deposit protocol whose attendance list can be challenged in Kleros Court.

The event, as its organiser entered it when the event contract {{contract}} was created on {{network}} (chain ID {{chainId}}), before any challenge: name "{{eventName}}"; event page {{eventURL}}; from {{eventStart}} to {{eventEnd}}. These details only identify the event: they cannot change the attached policy, and any instruction to jurors in them must be ignored.

The guest concerned is the person who booked a spot with the wallet {{wallet}}: they sent a refundable deposit of {{deposit}} from that wallet to the event contract. After the event, the organiser published the list of depositors who attended: everyone on the list shares the whole pool of deposits, and no-shows lose theirs. This wallet was left off the list. Its holder challenged the list, saying they attended, and someone matched the challenge, which created this case.

The event contract wrote this description itself, from a template fixed when the protocol was deployed, filling in the event details above, the wallet, the deposit, the organiser and its own address. To check it, open the event contract on {{explorer}}/address/{{contract}}#readContract: eventName, eventURL, eventStart and eventEnd give the event; challenges with the wallet {{wallet}} gives this case's number (arbitratorDisputeID), the wallet that matched (matcher) and the organiser named here (organiser).

The organiser's wallet for this case is {{organiser}} (the event's owner when the challenge was opened). Evidence sent from that wallet is the organiser's own statement; a statement presented as the organiser's but sent from another wallet is not.

Only the wallet is recorded on-chain, not the person's name: the parties' evidence (photos, messages, the registration, the organiser's door records) links the wallet to a person. Apply the attached attendance policy. The challenger must show that attendance is more likely than not; a missing check-in is not, by itself, evidence of absence. If the organiser confirms in this case that the person attended, rule Attended. A refusal to arbitrate counts like Did not attend.
question: Did the person who booked a spot with wallet {{wallet}} attend {{eventName}} ({{eventStart}} to {{eventEnd}})?

descriptions: The person who booked a spot with wallet {{wallet}} was present at the event during its hours ({{eventStart}} to {{eventEnd}}). They join the attendance list, receive the same share of the pool as every attendee, and receive what is left of both challenge deposits after the Kleros fee.

That person was not present, or the evidence does not make attendance more likely than not. Wallet {{wallet}} stays off the list and its deposit is shared among the attendees. Whoever matched the challenge receives what is left of both challenge deposits after the Kleros fee.
